$comment: Dev OS automated cycle configuration. Changing a model id is a D-row.

builder.effort_note: The reviewer sets 'Effort: low|medium|high|xhigh' and 'Fast: yes|no' in each fence header; scripts/devos/builder-model.mjs turns that into a Cursor model id (grok-4.7-<effort>[-fast]) and checks it against `agent models`, falling back to `model`.
builder.model_note: Cursor documents only the family id grok-4.7 (default effort high, Fast the default speed on Pro). The effort/fast ids the CLI accepts come from `agent models` on your account; each run records the Grok ids it offered in the PR's runner evidence.
builder.slices_note: agent-watchdog.sh: a build runs in 72-minute time slices; a slice that ends while files are still changing is committed and the same attempt continues in a fresh run, up to max_time_slices. Nothing changing for idle_stop_minutes = stuck (restarted once, then halted). Live progress: scripts/devos/progress.sh on the devos:notices issue.

reviewer.model_note: Official Claude ids (claude-opus-5-5, claude-sonnet-5-5). Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 default to medium effort in Claude Code, so the runner always passes --effort. --fallback-model only applies when the primary is overloaded or unavailable, never on usage limits.
reviewer.review_note: PR-22, evidence-first review: the builder does the work and proves it, the runner runs every check and writes .devos/evidence.md, and the reviewer judges that evidence. scripts/devos/review-mode.mjs picks the mode after the build: light (risk 1-2, nothing critical touched) or deep (risk 3, a gate, or a deep_paths file in the diff). A retry raises the effort one step.

screens.$comment: Default pages when the fence has no - Screens: line. filmstrip_ms and settle_max_ms are written into .devos/screens/motion.json. Signed-in pages need the M3 fixture states (DEVOS_SCREENS=1).

builder_method.$comment: PR-28: a method fix (Phase PM) may change workflows, runner scripts, guards, prompts and this config; never the product, the reviewer's own rules or the ledgers. The workflow from main forces the deep review and the human gate.

resume.relay_note: PR-31: waits longer than inline_wait_max_minutes are relayed by devos-wait (public: only on public repositories, where runner minutes are free; always; never). A limit that states no reset time is retried after default_wait_minutes, doubling on each repeat up to max_backoff_minutes.

modules.$comment: Optional stack modules (PR-17). A module is active when its detect file exists in the tree; its checks then join required_checks.

supabase.env_note: Names the app reads, mapped from `supabase status -o env`. Local keys are the CLI's throwaway demo keys; production values live only in Vercel and GitHub secrets.

r2.$comment: PR-26. Object storage (Cloudflare R2) through the S3 API. Active when the server-only storage code exists. Every run gets a throwaway S3-compatible store in Docker (scripts/devos/r2.mjs).
r2.env_note: Locally they point at the emulator with throwaway keys (.devos/r2.env). In production: Vercel Production env (the two keys marked sensitive) and the same five as GitHub secrets for the deploy's storage preflight. R2_ENDPOINT is https://<account-id>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com; R2_PUBLIC_BASE_URL is the bucket's public URL (r2.dev until the product has a custom domain).

firebase.$comment: PR-26. Cloud Firestore as a server-read content store, seeded from firebase/seed/*.json. Active when firebase.json exists. Every run gets the Firestore emulator under a demo project id (scripts/devos/firebase.mjs).
firebase.env_note: Locally FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID=demo-devos and FIRESTORE_EMULATOR_HOST point at the emulator (.devos/firebase.env); no credentials exist. Production: Vercel holds FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID and FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT (a read-only key, sensitive); GitHub holds FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID and FIREBASE_DEPLOY_SERVICE_ACCOUNT for rules and seed. client_sdk false: the browser never talks to Firebase (no firebase/* web SDK; rules deny every client).

heavy.$comment: PR-20. A run is heavy when its review uses reviewer.gate_model or xhigh effort, or its fence builds at xhigh. Repository variable DEVOS_HEAVY: notify (default) announces it in the 'Dev OS: run notices' issue; hold also waits for '/devos go' before a heavy task's first attempt.

retry_build_on: next/font/google queries have exactly one entry|turbopack-next/internal/font/google|Failed to fetch .*Google Fonts|fonts\.googleapis\.com.*(ETIMEDOUT|ECONNRESET|fetch failed)
retry_build_note: PR-24: a build failure whose log matches retry_build_on is the Google Fonts download, not the code; run-checks and devos-deploy retry it up to 3 times.

supervisor.note: devos-supervisor.yml + scripts/devos/supervisor.mjs: notices stopped or stalled work, explains it with fixed rules (Claude, read-only, only when none fits), fixes what is safe (re-run, resume, continue, recover a rescue branch, start the next task) at most max_auto_per_key times per cause, and turns everything else into an issue, a proposal (/devos approve <id>) or setup steps. Never merges, pushes to main or handles a secret. Off: variable DEVOS_SUPERVISOR=off.

registry.$comment: PR-61: the DEV_OS registry's address, the audience of the OIDC token the report job sends. Empty: nothing is sent.

structure.$comment: PR-58: the product's feature modules. Each is a folder with a public entry; code outside a module imports it only through that entry (guard:imports). The blueprint writes modules in devos/project.json from stack.scaffold.modules; aliases name import prefixes the guard resolves besides tsconfig.json paths; exempt files (tests) may reach inside a module.

stack.$comment: PR-48: the stack devos init chose. node runs package.json scripts with pnpm, as before; any other toolchain runs these commands once its manifest exists. PR-51: preview serves the production build for screens.mjs ({port} is replaced, PORT is set); empty means next start.
